correctness.rationale: The mutual-comparability relation is an equivalence relation, with a well-defined quotient poset and positive integer class sizes; expansion and weighted quotient preserve exactly isomorphism types. Independently enumerated quotient posets by entire minimal-antichain removal/reinsertion, expanded the positive weights by cut positions, and refined with full atomic pair types including equality and mutual comparability. Exact isomorphism within each joint-profile class gives totals 1,3,9,33,139,718,4535,35979, the same class totals through seven, and 35977 classes at eight, consisting of 35975 singleton classes and two doubletons without any distinct mutually comparable elements. Refinement computes unary counting types inductively: all two-name binary formulas combine atomic pair data and unary or nullary quantified subformulas. Every n-element local partition stabilizes after at most n−1 rounds; one more shared round records the per-class type counts needed to match stable cells across two structures. Thus the bounded rounds suffice for unrestricted C², even if the entire global palette has not stabilized. The two pairs of frozen codes have the stated different component and cover counts. Specialization translates finite topologies exactly to preorders; T₀ corresponds to antisymmetry, and cardinality sentences rule out collisions at different orders.
residual_risks: Exhaustion applies only through order eight and only to the specified signature/class, not to all finite relational structures or to larger non-T₀ spaces.

value.rationale: The finite-topology/preorder correspondence motivates counting equivalence classes of a natural logic on a natural class, with no arbitrary sampling. It is useful to know that the first loss of identification creates exactly the two known T₀ obstructions and that none of the 18980 non-T₀ eight-point types participates. This is a complete first-layer census and a sharp distinction between the topological and antisymmetric domains, not merely a new computation of the known isomorphism table.
residual_risks: No broader identification theorem for arbitrary non-T₀ spaces follows from this finite census.
